why: The first draft of the initials ticket, which the real evaluator scored 4.43. It is good but leaves null input, validation order and non-letter first characters undecided. Reasonable reviewers could go either way, so it is used to measure how much the score moves, not counted as right or wrong.

task.summary: Add an initials(name) helper to the text utilities that turns a person's name into upper-case initials, for use in avatar placeholders.

story.role: a developer building a user list
story.want: a helper that turns a full name into its initials
story.benefit: avatar placeholders show consistent initials without each screen re-implementing the rule

impactedAreas.area: Public API of the text utilities (src/index.js)
impactedAreas.impact: Gains one new export, initials. No existing export changes, so current callers are unaffected.
The list of functions should mention initials.

task.goal: Add initials(name) to the text utilities so callers can derive upper-case initials from a person's name.

acceptance.behavior: The first letter of each whitespace-separated word is returned, upper-cased, in order.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "ada lovelace"
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "AL"

acceptance.behavior: Leading, trailing and repeated whitespace between words is ignored.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "  grace   brewster  hopper "
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "GBH"

acceptance.behavior: A name with a single word returns one initial, and an empty or blank name returns the empty string.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "plato"
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "P"
And given the name "   "
When initials is called with it
Then the result is ""

acceptance.behavior: An optional second argument, max, limits how many initials are returned, keeping the first ones. It must be a positive integer.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "grace brewster hopper" and max 2
When initials is called with them
Then the result is "GB"
And given max 0, -1, 1.5 or "2"
When initials is called with any name
Then a RangeError is thrown

acceptance.behavior: initials is exported from src/index.js alongside the existing functions.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a module that imports initials from src/index.js
When it calls initials("ada lovelace")
Then the result is "AL"

testCases.description: initials("ada lovelace") returns "AL"; initials("Ada Lovelace") also returns "AL".
initials("  grace   brewster  hopper ") returns "GBH"; a name separated by a tab and a newline, "a\tb\nc", returns "ABC".
initials("plato") returns "P"; initials("") and initials("   ") both return "".
initials("grace brewster hopper", 2) returns "GB"; with max 5 it returns "GBH"; with max omitted it returns "GBH".
initials("a b", bad) throws RangeError for each bad value in 0, -1, 1.5, NaN and the string "2".
The test file imports initials from ../src/index.js, so every test fails if the export is missing.

scenarios.omitted: Hidden scenarios are not implemented yet.

nonGoals: Handling titles or suffixes such as "Dr" or "Jr"
Treating hyphenated or apostrophe names specially: "mary-jane" is one word and gives "M"
reuse: The argument validation style in src/truncate.js, which throws RangeError for an invalid max
task.approach: One small module in the same style as the existing ones: plain JavaScript, a named export, a JSDoc comment, and its own test file using node:test.
